html:
A lawyer who led Mauritania to independence from France on 28 November 1960 and was its president until a military coup in July 1978.

Morocco claimed Mauritania at first and blocked its UN seat until 1961. Ould Daddah built a state from scratch, with a new capital at Nouakchott, an Islamic republic and a one-party system. In 1973 he left the CFA franc for a national currency, the ouguiya, and he nationalised the iron mines. In 1975 he agreed to split Western Sahara with Morocco, which brought the Polisario Front into the war against his country. The cost of the war led to his overthrow. A long line of military rulers followed.
sum: A lawyer who led Mauritania to independence from France on 28 November 1960 and was its president until a military coup in July 1978.
